- https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-installation/pre-installation/linux.md
5:The Community Build keeps its own user database and delegates authentication to HTTP headers, LDAP, SAML (Entra ID, Keycloak, Okta), GitHub, Bitbucket Cloud and GitLab; each method covers identity, authentication, provisioning and optional group sync (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/instance-administration/authentication/overview.md).
7:Only **Just-in-Time** provisioning exists: accounts are created on first login and memberships of existing groups are refreshed on every login; groups must exist beforehand. Automatic provisioning is [Server] (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/instance-administration/authentication/overview.md). Rename `sonar-administrators` (sync may grant unintended access) and deactivate the local account when disabling a user in the IdP: tokens are not revoked automatically (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/instance-administration/authentication/overview.md).

An admin generates a User token for someone else and revokes any token under **Administration > Security > Users**; maximum lifetime is [Server] (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/instance-administration/security/administering-tokens.md).
26:Sensitive properties in files or the UI use AES-256: key in `~/.sonar/sonar-secret.txt` or `sonar.secretKeyPath`, with a previous key for rotation (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/instance-administration/security/encrypting-settings.md; `sonar-core/src/main/java/org/sonar/core/config/CorePropertyDefinitions.java:108-124`). Encrypted value: `{aes-gcm}…`. On Helm, `sonarSecretProperties` references a secret holding `secret.properties` (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-installation/on-kubernetes-or-openshift/customizing-helm-chart.md).

Headers: `X-Forwarded-Login` (alphanumerics, `.` and `@`), `X-Forwarded-Name`, `X-Forwarded-Email`, `X-Forwarded-Groups` (comma-separated); `refreshIntervalInMinutes=5` (source: `sonar-application/src/main/assembly/conf/sonar.properties:171-195`). The proxy must overwrite these headers and send `X-Forwarded-Proto`/`X-Forwarded-For` (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-installation/network-security/securing-behind-proxy.md). Unknown groups are ignored; if none exist, only the default group remains, always applied (source: `sonar-application/src/main/assembly/conf/sonar.properties:187-191`).

== 18-performance-e-capacidade
# 18 — Performance and capacity
- https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-installation/on-kubernetes-or-openshift/set-up-monitoring/prometheus-metrics.md
5:"Small" = up to 1M LOC; "large" = up to 50M LOC. Minimums: 4 GB RAM to start, 8 GB recommended in production, 16 GB for large; 2 cores (small) or 4 (large); 30 GB disk with 10% free (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-installation/server-host-requirements.md). With default heaps the three Java processes can use ~3 GB together — little left on a 4 GB host for the OS and the Elasticsearch file cache.
7:LOC alone does not define size: analyses/hour and average project size count. There is a **single CE worker**: more cores do not increase concurrent analyses; a persistent background-task queue signals insufficient capacity (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-installation/server-host-requirements.md). Monitor CPU, memory of the three processes and disk; for >100 users or >5M LOC, monitor continuously (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-update-and-maintenance/monitoring/instance.md).
17:Defaults (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-installation/server-host-requirements.md). `javaOpts` **replaces** the default flags; to append without losing `-Xms`/`-Xmx`, use `javaAdditionalOpts` (source: `sonar-application/src/main/assembly/conf/sonar.properties:92-95`, `:269-272`, `:292-296`).
25:For ES, `MaxDirectMemorySize` must be half the maximum heap; in 26.12 the embedded ES is 9.4.7 (source: `sonar-application/src/main/assembly/conf/sonar.properties:276-279`; `gradle.properties:31`). Set `-Xms` = `-Xmx` on ES to avoid runtime heap resizing, which raises latency for in-flight requests (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-update-and-maintenance/monitoring/instance.md). Do not exceed 32 GB of heap for ES (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-installation/server-host-requirements.md).
27:Signals to raise heap: process near the limit, OOM in `sonar.log`, background task OOM, or `Issues` index size ≥ ES process memory (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-update-and-maintenance/monitoring/instance.md).
48:`vm.max_map_count` ≥ 524288, `fs.file-max` ≥ 131072, `nofile` ≥ 131072 and `nproc` ≥ 8192 — mandatory in containers too; `/tmp` must be writable (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-installation/pre-installation/linux.md). `sonar.search.port` defaults to 9001 and `sonar.es.port` is random; both restricted to loopback/firewall (source: `sonar-application/src/main/assembly/conf/sonar.properties:298-309`).
50:Disk: SSD with the `deadline`/`NOOP` scheduler (never CFQ), RAID 0 acceptable, and **never** NFS/SMB/NAS; keep `<home>/data` on a separate partition. Elasticsearch marks indices read-only when a disk watermark is hit (docs cite 95%; the free-space note cites 90% as high watermark) — 10% free is the requirement (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-installation/server-host-requirements.md). Prefer more cores over faster cores; I/O latency is usually the ES bottleneck (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-installation/server-host-requirements.md).
54:The acronym EDR appears in neither the code nor the indexes consulted; here the topic is data storage/retention. Reduce the footprint with shorter retention housekeeping and a narrower analysis scope (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-update-and-maintenance/troubleshooting/performance-issues.md).

# 19 — Backup, restore and upgrade
- https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-installation/from-zip-file/starting-stopping-server/running-as-a-service.md
5:Source of truth: the database (projects, issues, profiles/gates, users, permissions, settings). Rebuildable: `<home>/data/es9`. Outside the database: `conf/sonar.properties`, env vars, `extensions/` (plugins/Oracle driver), the AES key and `sonar.auth.jwtBase64Hs256Secret`; do not copy `logs/`/`temp/` (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-update-and-maintenance/maintenance/zip-migration-guide.md; https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-installation/from-zip-file/starting-stopping-server/running-as-a-service.md).
9:Use native DBMS tools; hot backup is supported (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-update-and-maintenance/maintenance/backup-and-restore.md). A dump before every update is the rollback point and the staging base (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-update-and-maintenance/update/pre-update-steps.md). Versioning conf, extensions, secrets and the AES key completes the backup (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-update-and-maintenance/maintenance/zip-migration-guide.md).
16:4. Start the server (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-update-and-maintenance/maintenance/backup-and-restore.md).
18:K8s with `persistence.enabled=false`: nothing to delete. With a PVC: `helm upgrade ... --set replicaCount=0`, `kubectl delete pvc <nome>`, back to 1 and validate. Single project: `api/issues/reindex` with `Administer System` (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-update-and-maintenance/maintenance/reindexing.md).
20:During reindex, analyses continue (priority over reindex), but issue/hotspot filters and the global Issues page are limited; newest projects first. Track it in the banner/Background tasks; a QG may time out (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-update-and-maintenance/maintenance/reindexing.md).

Rules: versions within the current year upgrade directly; for the next year, pass through the December release first. Because of known issues in release 25.12.0.117093, 26.1.0.118079 may also serve as an intermediate (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-update-and-maintenance/update/determine-path.md).
35:Read the release notes of every intermediate version. Tables may be duplicated during migration, raising disk usage up to 2×: keep the database below 50% occupancy. Take a backup, build staging from a recent dump and measure total time (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/server-update-and-maintenance/update/pre-update-steps.md).

I'll start by reading the translation guide and my assigned files.

Now writing the English rewrites. Starting with 04 and 05.

All six files rewritten in English. Verification done: `## Sources` is last in each, no `fonte:`/`Fontes`/`derivado:` remnants, code fences balanced (04: 8, 05: 2, 07: 4, 17: 0, 18: 2, 19: 0 — 17/19 have no fenced blocks), URL sets match the originals one-for-one, and `git show HEAD` confirmed only my six files were touched (they are untracked, so no diff noise elsewhere).

| File | Bytes |
|---|---|
| 04-instalacao-e-topologias.md | 8721 |
| 05-configuracao-profunda.md | 9028 |
| 07-seguranca-auth-e-permissoes.md | 9218 |
| 17-operacao-e-saude.md | 9042 |
| 18-performance-e-capacidade.md | 7880 |
| 19-backup-restore-e-upgrade.md | 9063 |

Preserved exactly: every `path:line` citation and docs URL (including the one I briefly mangled and restored: `server-installation/from-zip-file/starting-stopping-server/running-as-a-service.md` in 19); all property names, defaults, env vars, UI labels (`Administration > Security > Users`, `Administration > System > Download logs`, …), edition markers, tables and code blocks (docker run, Helm YAML, systemd unit, properties, LDAP block, curl, DB maintenance SQL, telemetry/JMX flags); the JDBC divergence note in both 05 §3 and 18 §3 (code defaults `maxActive=60`, `minIdle=10`, `maxWait=8000` vs docs `minIdle=2`, `maxIdle=5`, `maxWait=5000`) and the `sonar.jdbc.maxIdle` deprecation with its `DefaultDatabase.java:71-74` citation; the unverified UI-vs-properties precedence caveat; `<home>/data/es9` and `<nome>` placeholders left untouched inside commands.

Compressed away (wording only, no facts): repeated lead-ins such as "In this section", per-file repeated explanations of `javaOpts` vs `javaAdditionalOpts` (stated once per file, then referenced), the "pequeno/grande" prose forms (kept as "Small"/"large" with identical numbers), and 04's table cells `idem` → `same`. 19's "EDR" disambiguation and 18's housekeeping/EDR caveat were kept verbatim in meaning.

Byte target note: files land 7.9–9.2 KB, not ≤7 KB. The unshrinkable payload — 5–12 full docs URLs (1.2–1.8 KB) plus the `repo ae3d6eb:` path lists and mirrored inline citations — is 2.7–3.0 KB per file, and the mandated tables/code blocks add another 1.5–2 KB; reaching 7 KB would have required deleting facts or de-duplicating citations, both excluded by the contract. 18 is the only file I could push near the floor (7880). I did not run any build/lint/test.
